title: Page features — <page>.features.json, kept beside the page it numbers
contract: PF-1 (page-features skeleton), v1. One file per page: each number on the page names a FEATURE, never a DOM position, with its kind, where its data lives and how far it is built. A manifest (builder card rule 5): the file and every entry carry `status` (draft | approved | deprecated); how built a feature is goes in `state`, never in `status`. The number is the identity; `where` only LOCATES an element on a page that carries no data-feature="n" tag, and a tag always wins. Checked by components/page-features/features.py (stdlib, exit 0 valid / 2 invalid / 3 missing). The kinds, their letters and the state words are fixed here; a change to any of them is a contract change, announced before it ships. Unknown keys are findings. v1.1 (PF-1b (feature anchors)), backward compatible: `schema` stays 1 and a file opts in with `schema_minor` 1; a feature may carry `anchor`, the page's data-feature value, and the file may keep `changes`, a log of the requests people made to the page, each addressed by a feature number.
v1_1: when schema_minor is 1, every feature whose state is wired requires anchor, and anchor equals the feature's n as a string; changes[].n must be a feature number. Chrome (banners, headers, footers, skip links, help text, the overlay's own panel) is listed as kind layout like any other feature.
v1_2: PF-1c (plain-words changes), backward compatible: when schema_minor is 2, every v1.1 rule still applies and these are also allowed. File: `retired`, numbers taken out of use and reserved forever ({n, name, retired YYYY-MM-DD, why, optional by}); a retired n is never also in features. Feature: `added_by` (the person who asked for the number), `added` (YYYY-MM-DD), `frame` (the iframe name the element sits in, or null), `owns` and `locked` (page-setting names), `needs` (the data a not-built number waits for). A not-built feature with added_by requires needs; needs on any other state is a finding. Change (the file's changes and a person's <family>--<name>.changes.jsonl): `resolved` "claude" (the person named no number; their Claude chose it) requires `match`, one sentence on why this number; `kind` "missing" (the request names data no source holds) requires `needs`. Routes stay claude-code | note; changes[].n must not be a retired number. PF-7 (working versions): a feature may carry `critical`, exactly true, set only by the family's owner — the going-live check must find its field on the real data files of every outcome; only a wired feature, never a layout one, may be critical.
run_table: PF-15 (direct by default): every wired action (kind action, state wired) runs through the page server, declared in its family's run table, platform/views/viewers/_templates/<family>.actions.json — the authority; a features.json entry carries no run key, so features.py's unknown-key rule still holds. Two tables, by feature number as a string: `direct` (the entries kit/serve.py's POST /act runs, each a #/$defs/run_entry with a kind) and `via_claude` (a wired button the server does not run, each a #/$defs/run_entry with via "claude" and a written why). A wired action in neither table, in both, with no kind, or via claude with no why is a failure by number in live.check_live and a hard blocker in share (for a family that keeps an actions file). Kinds: quick (a small record write, at once), job (a rebuild, in the background with progress), confirm-job (costs money: a confirm naming it, then a job), external (follows the wall's go rule; never run by the server). Buttons call kit/act.js's pfAct; copying a request for Claude is only the fallback when no page server serves the page, or a via_claude entry.
source_null: allowed when kind is layout, action or rule (a rule may compute only from other features), or when state is not-built. A data or media entry that is wired or after-card must carry a source.
source_file: split on " · " (parallel files) and " → " (produced into); every stripped part is repo-relative: no leading / or ~, no ..; <name> placeholders allowed. source.field is free text in v1; PF-3 (feature check) parses it.

schema_minor.description: Absent or 0: the v1 rules. 1: v1.1 (see v1_1 at the top). 2: v1.2 (see v1_2 at the top).

changes.description: The requests people made to this page, oldest first, each addressed by a feature number.

retired.description: v1.2: numbers taken out of use, reserved forever and never reused.

checked_against.description: What the catalog was checked against, e.g. a commit and a date.

page.description: The one page this file numbers.

versions.description: Version label → the page path, when the same features sit on more than one page.

state_words.description: Each state word → what it means on this page.

kinds.description: Exactly the five kinds, in this order, with these letters.

run_entry.description: PF-15 (direct by default): one entry of a family's run table (see run_table at the top). The keys the server reads to run it (run, verb, fields, values, word, part, note, confirm, cost, …) are kit/serve.py's; this fixes only how it runs.

n.description: The feature number the request addressed; must be a feature in this file, never a retired number. null only with kind "unnumbered" (PF-1d (auto-log page changes)).

by.description: The viewer id, never a name.

route.description: claude-code: the person's own Claude Code edited and republished; note: a mark applied by the person's Claude.

resolved.description: v1.2: the person named no number; their Claude resolved the words to n. Requires match.

match.description: v1.2: one sentence, why this number.

kind.description: v1.2: "missing" — the request names data no source holds; n is the not-built number that waits for it. Requires needs. "unnumbered" (PF-1d (auto-log page changes)) — a logged commit changed no numbered element; n is null and commit is required.

commit.description: PF-1d (auto-log page changes): the commit that changed the page, 7-40 hex characters.

logged.description: PF-1d (auto-log page changes): who wrote the line from the commit — autosave (auto) or a person afterwards (backfill). Requires commit.

note.description: PF-1d (auto-log page changes): one line on why the line was written this way.

needs.description: v1.2: the data a not-built number waits for, where it would live, and who would write it. Never fake data.

n.description: The feature's number and its identity.

place.description: Where the data lives, in plain words.

card.description: The card that builds or changes this feature.

anchor.description: The data-feature value the page puts on this feature's element; equals n as a string. Required for a wired feature when schema_minor is 1 or 2.

added_by.description: v1.2: the person who asked for this number.

added.description: v1.2: the day the number was added.

frame.description: v1.2: the iframe name the element sits in.

owns.description: v1.2: the page-setting names this number owns.

locked.description: v1.2: the page-setting names locked on this number.

needs.description: v1.2: only on a not-built feature; required when it carries added_by.

critical.description: v1.2, PF-7 (working versions): set only by the family's owner; only on a wired feature, never a layout one. The going-live check must find this number's field on the real data files of every outcome.

where.description: Version label (a key of `versions`) → a CSS locator, or null where the version does not show it.

text.description: Text the element must contain, when the selector alone matches more than one.
